Script: app.open("C:/Program Files/Adobe/Adobe Illustrator 2026/Presets/en_US/Brushes/Artistic/Artistic_Watercolor.ai"), doc.brushes.getByName("Watercolor Stroke 4 ").applyTo(pathItem) on a path in that document, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) (the brush arrives in the target document), then close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES. The harvested name carries 1 trailing space(s); getByName needs the exact string.

verified.note: Charcoal-grey layered stroke, darkest of the set, rough dark start and a tail split into streaks, as described.

cards.name: Watercolor Stroke 5
cards.summary: Art brush from Artistic_Watercolor. A dark-to-mid grey stroke of fairly even medium width with layered bands: a darker core, a softer, lighter halo along the edges, a blunt start and a tapered end. (Thumbnail: the brush applied by script to a 300 pt S-curve with a 1 pt stroke in its library document, not a shipped preview.)
avoid: broken, dry texture: Watercolor Stroke 3 or 2

relying on it to take your stroke colour: on the scripted 1 pt stroke it rendered in greys; whether it recolours depends on the brush's Colorization option (not checked), so test or recolour after Object > Expand Appearance
very short or hairpin paths: an Art brush stretches its whole stroke art along the path, so tapers and textures distort on tight bends

cards.name: Watercolor Stroke 6
cards.summary: Art brush from Artistic_Watercolor. A mid-grey, medium-wide watercolour stroke with a ragged, blunt start (a pale spot sits inside its darker edge), layered darker and lighter grey bands along the body, and a tapering, slightly split end. (Thumbnail: the brush applied by script to a 300 pt S-curve with a 1 pt stroke in its library document, not a shipped preview.)
use_for: painted swashes with a distinctive start
avoid: symmetric strokes: the ragged, blunt start and the tapered end look very different

relying on it to take your stroke colour: on the scripted 1 pt stroke it rendered in greys; whether it recolours depends on the brush's Colorization option (not checked), so test or recolour after Object > Expand Appearance
very short or hairpin paths: an Art brush stretches its whole stroke art along the path, so tapers and textures distort on tight bends

cards.name: Cut Here
cards.summary: Pattern brush from Borders_Dashed: a fine black dashed line of short, evenly spaced dashes that follows the path smoothly. No scissors or other symbol appears on the scripted S-curve; it is plain dashes, meant (by its name) as a cut line. (Thumbnail: the brush applied by script to a 300 pt S-curve with a 1 pt stroke in its library document, not a shipped preview.)
avoid: needing an editable dash pattern: a plain stroke with Stroke panel > Dashed Line is easier to tune
expecting a scissors icon: none showed on the scripted path
cards.applies_to: a stroked path item, open or closed; a Pattern brush (Adobe PatternOnPath Brush Tool / Pattern Brush Plugin) that repeats its tile along the path instead of stretching one piece of art, so long paths keep the same dash size; the stroke weight scales the tiles. The brush must exist in the target document.
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: Window > Brush Libraries > Borders > Borders_Dashed, select a path, click 'Cut Here'. verified.note: Fine black line of short, evenly spaced dashes following the curve, no scissors symbol, as described.
